blind_target.authors: Smith, T. R., Panfil, K., & Kirkpatrick, K.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
Experimental work investigating possible causal rela-

tions between impulsive choice and extended experience

with immediate reinforcement is limited, but some work

suggests that experience with immediate reinforcement

may subsequently increase impulsive choice or blunt matu-

rational decreases in impulsive choice in a delay-discounting
paradigm (Fox, 2022; Fox etal., 2019; Renda etal., 2018;

Smith etal., 2022). It was the goal of the work presented

here to expand on this body of research by testing eﬀects

of an immediate reinforcement intervention that was 50%

longer in duration, included approximately twice as many

immediate reinforcement training trials, and employed twice

the sample, than previous work. In doing so, we hoped to

test the limits and generality of previously reported results.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
A group of rats was exposed to an immediate (no-delay)-

reinforcement intervention and subsequent delay discounting

behavior was modestly, but statistically signiﬁcantly, more

impulsive compared to a control group. This is consistent

with previous work (Fox, 2022; Fox etal., 2019; Renda

etal., 2018; Smith etal., 2022), and with the conclusion
that prolonged exposure to immediate reinforcement may

have just modest impacts on subsequent impulsive choice,

compared to relatively larger impacts of exposure to delayed

reinforcement. This was true in the present experiment
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The introduction identifies the set of prior immediate-reinforcement findings whose generality is tested; the discussion explicitly reports consistency with every named member of that set. Modest magnitude is not framed as failure.
blind_target.title: Generalizability of time-based interventions: Effects of choice procedure and smaller-sooner delay
